mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% is interpreted by markets as a signal of tighter monetary policy, which raises discount rates and reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: In a regime where inflation is controlled below 2%, the 60-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), contradicting the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with rising consumer confidence (HOUST), creating a labor-market strength signal that anticipates positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During recessions where PAYEMS growth turns negative, the 20-day forward return is negative even when HOUST remains high.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 suggests weakening supply-side constraints, prompting investors to reallocate into growth equities and producing positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO shows no meaningful recovery over a 4-week window while SPX 5-day returns remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of demand (RSAFS) to supply (INDPRO) exceeds 1.1 for two consecutive months, it indicates an imbalance favoring demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: The condition holds but 20-day forward returns are negative in 3 out of 10 occurrences.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a risk-off reaction as investors anticipate tighter policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE remains above 4% in a low-inflation environment, the 20-day forward return is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising pay growth (PAYEMS) without a corresponding increase in inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal wage growth is outpacing costs, which supports consumer spending and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > CPIAUCSL inflation for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In high-inflation periods, the signal is present but 60-day returns are flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 10-year yield proxy (FEDFUNDS) below 3% for three months is interpreted as a forward guidance signal for continued easing, which is associated with positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The 10-year yield recovers above 3% before the 5-day return window ends, producing negative results.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) remains below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months in a deflationary regime, it signals persistent supply-side weakness that precedes negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO crosses above its 12-month MA and the 20-day return is positive.
